title: Integral scalar-constant constructible sheaves form a weak Serre subcategory
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Give $\mathcal O_E$ its valuation topology, form the condensed ring $\underline{\mathcal O_E}(S)=C(S,\mathcal O_E)$ on profinite sets [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and put $R_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ on the small pro-étale site of $X$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. In the category $\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], call $F$ constructible if it admits a finite locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification] on each stratum $T$ of which it is pro-étale locally $R_T\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}P$ with $P$ a finitely presented scalar $\mathcal O_E$-module [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Here finitely presented means that $P$ is the cokernel of a scalar matrix $\mathcal O_E^m\to\mathcal O_E^n$ for finite nonnegative integers $m,n$. The tensor means extension of the constant module sheaf along the constant-section map. Kernels and cokernels, computed in $\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$, of morphisms between such constructible sheaves are constructible. For any short exact sequence $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$ of $R_X$-module sheaves with $F'$ and $F''$ constructible, $F$ is constructible. No finite-type, separatedness, dimension or invertibility hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

proof.text: Construct explicitly the continuous ring isomorphism between the valuation integers of the given small embedded finite coefficient field and latticeCoefficientIntegers for its universe lift. The algebra equivalence WithAbs(O_E) to E preserves norms by Mathlib NormedAlgebra.norm_eq_spectralNorm. The DVR membership characterization identifies the integer subrings. Postcomposition and its inverse give the isomorphism of condensed ring objects; this is constructed on sections, not chosen from an existence theorem.

Restriction of scalars along an isomorphism preserves finite presentations: transport finite free modules and their presenting cokernels. The mapModComapIso and comapUpperStarIso comparisons commute this restriction with pullback from the point and restriction to cover members and strata. Transport each finite constant local model, keeping its cover and stratification. The inverse isomorphism proves the converse, including the affine-local branch of constructibility. Apply integralLfpConstantModelComparison to the lifted coefficient field, then transport local finite presentation along the same coefficient isomorphism. This identifies the original constant-model predicate with IsConstructibleModuleObject for the original integral coefficient object.

The given normed integral coefficient object integralCoeff is definitionally the padicIntegersRingObj for the embedded finite coefficient field. Apply integralConstructible_serre to obtain closure of IsConstructibleModuleObject under ambient kernels, cokernels and extensions. Convert the two input hypotheses and each conclusion using the predicate equivalence of the previous step. Mathlib prop_kernel, prop_cokernel and prop_X₂_of_shortExact give the required conjunction without changing any ambient module or short exact sequence.
